I found this more challenging than many recent Wednesdays - I actually thought I might need lookups or reveals to finish, but ultimately I managed to fill the grid on my own in a time some 20% longer than my average for the day. I caught onto the theme quite late - phonetic features are harder to spot when you're not a native speaker, and the initial lack of crosses hindered my efforts to grasp what was going on. I finally understood the Odin clue as I was writing a paragraph here to ask what it was about. I=eye... More phonetics. I don't think I've ever seen the term GIBBOUS in my life. Polish doesn't even feature an equivalent term, at all. We have specific terms for four phases of the moon, only: nów (new [moon]; nowy means new, in the masculine, which the moon is in Polish), pierwsza kwadra (first quarter), pełnia (full[moon]; pełny means full), and ostatnia kwadra (last/final quarter). I first learned the word PANACHE, or panaché to be exact, 30 years ago, as the French term for a mix of beer and carbonated lemonade. There is an interesting etymology behind all that: https://www.balancemedia.co.uk/2017/06/02/word-of-the-week-panache/ (the text mentions a mix of vegetables rather than one of beverages, but you get the idea). Do Americans really throw SURPRISE PARTies or is it just a TV thing? I've never encountered a surprise party in Poland.

This message is meant as encouragement to newer puzzlers who might be intimidated by Wednesday puzzles. It is for all those people out there lurking like I do, reading how easy puzzles are becoming but still struggling or being challenged. 

Stick with it. Keep clicking through the crosses and downs and don't give up. I started last night and couldn't figure out the theme until this morning.  There were many clues that came to me after putting it away and coming back to it with a fresh perspective. 

I was finally able to complete it this morning. Six months or one year ago, I would have turned on autocorrect but now my confidence has increased and Wednesday puzzles are my new favorite. 

I do attribute this to persistence but also to reading Wordplay Column everyday and to regular contributors here with all their insights.

Someday I hope to feel the same about Friday and Saturday puzzles.

Cute and easy.  All you have to do is say the clue word out loud and you've got it.  At least that's all we Americans have to do.  I'm wondering if the Brits, who enunciate most words better than we do, don't provide just the slightest hint of an "e" sound rather than an "i" sound in "market" and "ticket", et al.

I'm asking this because I've been watching a British art competition series called "Portrait Artist of the Year".  They all pronounce the word portrait as "portrayt", rather than "portrit."  To my American ear, it sounds a bit pretentious and arty, but it's not.  It's just the Brits being Brits.

Hebrew has two words for moon לבנה "ləvanah" and ירח "yareiakh". The former is feminine and is a form of the root for  "white". The latter is masculine and means both "moon" and "month". (All nouns in Hebrew are gendered.)
